options: Sticks the name price_paise on the value 29900, so the name can be used later
Makes price_paise a piece of text
questions.explain: = means 'stick this name on this value'. It's not the 'equals' of maths; checking equality is ==.

questions.q: What is the type of "29900" (with quotes)?
questions.explain: Anything in quotes is text, a str. Without quotes, 29900 is an int.

questions.q: A customer types 3 in the quantity box. Your code gets quantity_text = "3". What does quantity_text * 3 give?
questions.explain: Input is text, and str * int repeats the text. Convert first: int(quantity_text) * 3 gives 9.

questions.q: Why does Bazaar never store money as float?
options: floats are stored in binary and can be slightly off: 649 * 1.18 gives 765.8199999999999
questions.explain: Most decimal fractions can't be stored exactly in binary. Totals go wrong and == checks fail. Bazaar keeps whole paise in an int.
// gives the rupees (1531), % gives the paise (64), :, adds the comma, :02d pads paise to two digits. "₹" + price_paise is a TypeError.

options: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'three'
questions.explain: int() only understands digits. Python stops with a ValueError instead of guessing. Read the last line of the error first.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why build Decimal("0.18") from text, not Decimal(0.18)?
options: Decimal(0.18) copies the float's tiny error: 0.17999999999999999333...
questions.explain: The float 0.18 is already slightly off, and Decimal keeps that exact wrong value. From text, Decimal("0.18") is exactly 0.18.

questions.q: (Going deeper) old_price = price; then price = 899. What happens to old_price?
options: It still points to the old object (999): = moves only the name price
questions.explain: Assigning moves a name to a new object. ints never change, so the old object stays as it was, and old_price still points to it.
